text:
Ah, the wax. That glorious, solidified byproduct of petroleum refining that we have so cleverly repurposed as the centerpiece of our "adulting" aesthetic. It is the primary material of a candle, yes, but more importantly, it is the primary material of our collective delusion that we are living in a cozy, romantic drama rather than a slow-motion crisis of back pain and instant noodles.

We drape ourselves in the illusion of sophistication, lighting these little pillars of melted oil to simulate a "magical journey." How magical! The magic is that we have convinced ourselves that choosing between Chicken and Beef flavor instant noodles is a high-stakes culinary decision worthy of a Michelin star. We speak of "long-term planning" with the gravity of a CEO, when in reality, our five-year plan is just trying to remember if we left the stove on or if that weird noise is our spine finally giving up the ghost.

The candle doesn't just burn wax; it burns away the last remnants of our youth, leaving behind a pool of hot grease and the stark realization that "spontaneity" is now just a synonym for "impulse buying something on Amazon at 2 AM because we’re lonely." So here’s to the wax, the silent witness to our descent into a life where the biggest thrill is finding a matching sock in the dryer. Truly, adulthood is a blast.
